content: Care workers, HIV program managers, and individuals living with HIV were engaged in assessments to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of strategies for delivering HIV services. These assessments were conducted alongside updates to clinical guidelines, which included diagnostic questions that informed the development of these guidelines. The dissemination of this survey was supported by the HIV Coverage, Quality, and Impact Network (CQUIN). The results of these surveys were utilized to determine the acceptability and feasibility of the range of questions addressed. Additionally, an online survey and ten focus group discussions were conducted to explore psychosocial support interventions for adolescents and youth. Systematic reviews were performed to gather published evidence on resource use, including costing, cost-effectiveness, and affordability data. Representatives from national programs, who were part of the Guideline Development and External Review Group, provided insights into the resource implications within their respective countries. Before the Guideline Development Group meeting, a WHO staff member with expertise in global health and ethics reviewed the proposed areas of intervention. Key equity-related issues were outlined and presented to the group for consideration during the formulation of recommendations. The Guideline Development Group convened virtually from October 5 to 9, 2020, to update the recommendations. Using an electronic survey, the group ranked the importance of each systematic review outcome on a scale of 1 to 9, following the GRADE rating system. Systematic reviews and evidence-to-decision-making tables, prepared in accordance with the GRADE process, were shared in advance and presented during the meetings. A methodologist facilitated discussions, and all recommendations were made through consensus. Voting was not required, but the group had pre-agreed that a two-thirds majority would be necessary for any decision. The Guideline Development Group formulated good practice principles based on their knowledge of optimal approaches to delivering HIV services. These principles were informed by the absence of harm in the evidence base and the inapplicability of the evidence to formal GRADE assessment. Updated recommendations on service delivery for the treatment and care of people living with HIV were peer-reviewed. Draft guidelines were circulated to members of the Guideline Development Group and the External Review Group for feedback. The WHO Guideline Steering Group reviewed the comments and incorporated them into the final document, ensuring that any conflicts of interest from External Review Group members were duly considered. All external contributors to the guidelines, including members of the Guideline Development Group and the External Review Group, completed a WHO declaration of interests form in line with WHO policy for experts. A brief biography of each Guideline Development Group member was published on the WHO HIV website for 14 days before the first meeting, along with a description of the meeting's objectives. No public comments or objections were received. The responsible technical officer reviewed the declarations of interest forms and conducted a web-based search for each member of the Guideline Development Group to identify any potential competing interests. The results were shared with the WHO Guideline Steering Group, which reviewed the findings and agreed on a management plan for each individual. At the start of the guideline development meeting, all identified conflicts of interest and their management plans were shared with the participants. In accordance with the revised WHO policy for experts, a web-based search was conducted to identify any potential competing interests among Guideline Development Group members. The WHO Guideline Steering Group recorded and reviewed the results of this search. Declared conflicts of interest were summarized and presented at the start of the Guideline Development Group meeting, and members were asked to disclose any additional or undeclared conflicts. One member of the 2020 Guideline Development Group, who led one of the systematic reviews informing the meeting, was excluded from voting on the corresponding recommendation. No other conflicts of interest warranted exclusion from the discussion of specific recommendations. The responsible technical officers reviewed the declaration of interest forms from members of the External Review Group in accordance with WHO guideline development policy. The results were shared with the WHO Guideline Steering Group. Any identified conflicts of interest were considered when interpreting comments from External Review Group members during the external review process.
